title: Complete Fertilizer 14 14 14: What Triple 14 Does and When to Use It
metaTitle: Complete Fertilizer 14 14 14: Uses, Timing and Grades
metaDescription: Complete fertilizer 14 14 14 gives equal nitrogen, phosphate and potash. See how triple 14 compares with 16 16 16 and 20 20 20, and when to apply it.
excerpt: Complete fertilizer 14 14 14 is a common basal abono for palay and mais in the Philippines. Farmers call it triple 14. It holds equal parts nitrogen, phosphate and potash, so one bag feeds all three main nutrients at planting. Here is what the numbers mean, how it compares with 16 16 16 and 20 20 20, and when to apply it.

heroImage.alt: Three kinds of fertilizer side by side in an open sack, the nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium that complete fertilizer 14 14 14 combines
heroImage.credit: Mahsa 110, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

blocks.text:
At the agri supply, many farmers just ask for 'complete'. The word means the bag carries all three major nutrients: nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium. It does not mean the bag has everything a crop needs. Zinc, for one, only comes in if the label says so.

The fertilizer picture at the top of this page shows three kinds of fertilizer poured side by side in one sack. A complete fertilizer saves you that mixing. It puts all three nutrients into one bag at a fixed grade, so every handful carries the same balance.
What the numbers on complete fertilizer 14 14 14 mean

The three numbers are the grade. They give the percent of nitrogen (N), phosphate (P2O5) and potash (K2O), always in that order. So 14 14 14 fertilizer is 14 percent of each.

In a 50 kg bag, that means 7 kg of nitrogen, 7 kg of phosphate and 7 kg of potash. The other 29 kg is the material that carries them, plus any extra nutrients on the label. Many brands on the FPA list of registered fertilizers also declare sulfur, often 8 or 11 percent. PhilRice notes that the sulfur in a 14 14 14 with sulfur is enough to correct the usual sulfur deficiency in rice.

blocks.title: Compound or blend
blocks.text: Some brands make compound granules, where each granule carries N, P and K. Others blend separate granules in one bag. The grade on the label holds either way, but a blend can separate in the bag, so mix it well before you spread.
Why triple 14 fertilizer goes on at planting

Phosphorus and potassium work early. IRRI says phosphorus drives root growth, tillering, early flowering and ripening. Its advice is to mix all the phosphorus into the soil before the last puddling, or within 10 to 15 days after direct seeding.

The PalayCheck guide of PhilRice times phosphorus at 0 to 14 days after transplanting (DAT), or 7 to 10 days after sowing (DAS). Most of the potassium and the first nitrogen dose fall in the same window. That is why a balanced bag like 14 14 14 makes a good basal fertilizer. The later nitrogen then comes from urea, the [46 0 0 fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer).
When to use complete fertilizer on rice, corn and vegetables
Palay

The Abonong Swak guide of PhilRice uses complete fertilizer as the basal dose in every plan. For a target of 3 to 4 tons per hectare, it calls for 1 bag of 14 14 14 per hectare at 0 to 14 DAT, or 10 to 14 DAS. For 5 to 8 tons, it calls for 2 bags in the same window. Urea and muriate of potash follow later, timed to the maturity of the variety.

Those plans also add rice straw and 10 bags of chicken manure or compost. Treat the numbers as a guide and adjust them to a soil test. Our [fertilizer for rice](/blog/fertilizer-for-rice) page lays out the whole season.
Mais

The corn guide of DA Regional Field Office 2 puts all the phosphorus and potassium, plus half the nitrogen, in the furrow at planting. It goes in a band about 5 cm beside and 5 cm below the seed. Complete fertilizer suits that job. The rest of the nitrogen goes on as a side dress 21 to 30 days after planting, during hilling up. See [pagtatanim ng mais](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-mais) for the full crop.
Vegetables

Vegetables take a balanced grade at planting too, but their needs shift as they flower. Yara, for example, recommends its 16 16 16 for early crop growth. For flowering and fruiting vegetables, it offers a grade higher in potassium. Follow the crop guide for your vegetable and a soil test. Our guide to [vegetables in the Philippines](/crops/vegetables-philippines) covers the common crops.
Complete fertilizer 14 14 14 vs 16 16 16 vs 20 20 20

blocks.text:
Fertilizer 16 16 16 simply packs more of each nutrient into a bag. So compare the price per kilo of nutrient, not per bag. A 16 16 16 bag carries 24 kg of nutrients against 21 kg for triple 14.

Fertilizer 20 20 20 is a different kind of product. Many 20 20 20 grades on the FPA list are water soluble or foliar feeds, like Peters Professional WSF. You dissolve them in water and spray them or run them through drip lines. A spray carries far less nutrient than a basal bag, so use it to top up a crop, not to replace the basal dose. More on sprays is in our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer).
Brands you will see: Atlas and Yara

Atlas Fertilizer Corporation is a Philippine maker. Its Atlas Perfect Gro 14 14 14 appears on the FPA list with 8 percent sulfur and 10 percent chloride. Atlas also sells Super Gro 16 20 0, urea and basal grades made for rice.

Yara Philippines sells compound fertilizer under the YaraMila name. YaraMila Unik 16 is its 16 16 16. The Yara Winner fertilizer, sold as YaraMila Winner, is a 15 9 20 with magnesium, sulfur, manganese, boron and zinc, and Yara pitches it for flowering and fruiting vegetables.

We do not favor any brand. Compare the grade, the extra nutrients, the price per kilo of nutrient and the FPA registration. Our guide to [fertilizer brands and dealers](/blog/fertilizer-brands-and-dealers) helps with that.
Price and how many bags to buy

The FPA dealer survey for September 14 to 18, 2026 put the national average for complete fertilizer at **PHP 1,902.92** per 50 kg bag. In the week of January 5 to 9, 2026 it was PHP 1,655.71. Prices change every week and differ by province, so check the FPA list before you buy.

The math is simple. The PhilRice plan for 5 to 6 tons per hectare uses 2 bags of 14 14 14. At the September average, that basal dose costs about PHP 3,805.84 per hectare. For a 1.5 hectare farm, buy 3 bags. Our [fertilizer calculation](/blog/fertilizer-calculation) guide shows how to do this for any grade.

blocks.text: Questions about complete fertilizer

items.q: What does 14 14 14 mean on a fertilizer bag?
items.a: It means 14 percent nitrogen, 14 percent phosphate and 14 percent potash. A 50 kg bag holds 7 kg of each.
Yes, as the basal dose. PhilRice plans apply 1 or 2 bags per hectare at 0 to 14 DAT, then follow with urea and muriate of potash.

items.q: What is the difference between 14 14 14 and 16 16 16?
items.a: Both are balanced. A bag of 16 16 16 holds 8 kg of each nutrient against 7 kg for 14 14 14, so compare the price per kilo of nutrient.

items.q: Can I use 20 20 20 instead of complete fertilizer?
items.a: Not as a basal dose. Many 20 20 20 products are water soluble feeds for spraying or drip. They top up a crop but carry too little nutrient to replace a basal bag.

items.q: How much is complete fertilizer 14 14 14 now?
items.a: The FPA national average for September 14 to 18, 2026 was PHP 1,902.92 per 50 kg bag. Prices change weekly, so check the FPA list for your province.
